   BOARD OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES MINUTES

  HEALTH DEPARTMENT TRAINING FACILITY, 7:45 AM

  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Van Meeveren, Red Eagle, Walton, Schwerin

  Alison King, Director of Health and Human Services, provided an update on the
  following:

  • Announced Retirement of Executive Assistant, Dennis Keith
  • Announced Alejandra Gutierrez – An internal employee from the Health and
  Human Services, Collective Impact Bureau as Dennis’ successor.
  • Thanked Board Member McNeeley for attending the Council District 8
  Meeting.
  • Boil Water Notice was put in place for the City of Long Beach residents in the
  90805, 90806, and 90807 zip codes.
  o A Boil Water Notice was placed out of precaution after a water main
  break occurred on Orange Ave and Wardlow Road on October 9,
  2024.
  o The notice was lifted on October 10, 2024, after water sample results
  cleared and were found to be within a safe range.
  o AlertLB Notification System was faulty and only alerted some of the
  residents in the affected area.
  o The Public Health Emergency Management Team was deployed.
  o Food facilities and restaurants were greatly affected, Environmental
  Health staff were providing advice and assistance to help ease the
  circumstances.
  • CDPP provided the City of Long Beach with a 457 million dollar grant to help
  with the local TB Emergency.
  • The Collected Impact Bureau was awarded 8 million dollars for violence
  prevention
  • Board member McNeely asked what The Health Department is doing
  regarding Prop One.
  o Currently looking for partnerships and accepting applications for
  grants with the NHHA.
  • Provided update on Loss of Funding; Out of 73 staff on the initial list, only 9
  remain and 2 are on leave.

3.  24-55172  Recommendation to receive and file a report from the City Health Officer.

  A motion was made by Member McNeeley, seconded by Member Lesen, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6 Clark, Gupta, Lesen, McNeeley, Tejani, Sanders
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None

  Page 2 of 4
   BOARD OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES MINUTES
  FRIDAY, OCTOBER 11, 2024
  3861 WORSHAM AVENUE
  HEALTH DEPARTMENT TRAINING FACILITY, 7:45 AM

  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Van Meeveren, Red Eagle, Walton, Schwerin

  Dr. Anissa Davis, City Health Officer, provided the following information to the
  Board:
  • Boil Water Notice was caused by a water main break causing a dip in water
  pressure.
  o Road access issues as the City works to fix the break.
  o Board Member Gupta asked about water bacteria levels; levels are
  within safe range.
  o Houghton Park and Summerset Park were used as water stations for
  residents.
  • Marburg Outbreak in Rwanda
  o CDC is implementing a level 3 Travel Advisory and will monitor all
  travelers returning from the area.
  o No treatment
  o High fatality rate.
  o Person to person transmission.
  • Bird flu
  o Three confirmed cases in Central California.
  o Animal to person transmission.

4.  24-55173  Recommendation to receive and file an update from the City’s Legislative Agenda.

  This agenda item was laid over by consensus to the next Board of Health and
  Human Services meeting.

5.  24-54387  Recommendation to submit a letter to the Mayor and City Council proposing that
  the City install beach water hazard signage along City waterways.

  The Board reviewed the letter to the Mayor and City Council proposing that the city
  install beach water hazard signage along the City waterways and had a brief
  discussion. The Board discussed the possibility of installing permanent signage to
  be inclusive of all residents. The Environmental Health Bureau currently test the
  water levels three times a week and City lifeguards post the signage along the
  waterways.

  A motion was made by Member Lesen, seconded by Member Gupta, to
  approve recommendation. The motion by the following vote:

  Yes:  6 Clark, Gupta, Lesen, McNeeley, Tejani, Sanders
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None

6.  24-55174  Recommendation to discuss Board Goals and Infrastructure.

  A motion was made by Member Lesen, seconded by Member Tejani, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Clark, Gupta, Lesen, McNeeley, Tejani, Sanders
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Van Meeveren, Red Eagle, Walton, Schwerin

  The Board discussed the following:
  • The Board subcommittee reviewed the Goals and Infrastructure Report
  created by Mr. James Suazo and broke them into smaller sub-discussions to
  be possibly added to the agenda.
  • Board Member Lesen asked about data accessibility regarding staffing
  shortages in the medical field.

PUBLIC COMMENT

There was no public comment.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

There were no announcements.

The meeting ended at 9:05 a.m.
